newsitem.title: USA: Musicland gets support from most vendors.
newsitem.headline: Musicland gets support from most vendors.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp said Thursday it continues to get financial support from most of its suppliers in the form of deferred payments.
The music and video specialty retailer also said it expects to regain normal credit terms from its vendors in September.

Musicland's sales and profits have been cut by price competition from non-mall based stores, and discount and consumer electronics stores. To restore profits, the company has implemented cost cutting measures, closed stores, tightened inventories and added more focused marketing.

"I don't think we would expect to (regain normal credit terms) until we get into the fall season," Musicland's chairman and chief executive officer Jack Eugster told shareholders at company's annual meeting here.
"We are having discussions and would expect to face that issue seriously in mid-to-late September as we start to build for Christmas," Eugster said.
"The vendors are still supporting us with trade payables. Almost all of them are shipping to us unimpeded," he added.
Last February, Musicland negotiated new payment terms with its suppliers and in June secured a $50 million term loan from lenders which can be drawn on September 15, 1997.
Eugster said Musicland will continue to close stores, although not as many as it had once anticipated.

"We will continue to close underperforming stores," Eugster said. "But in our Sam Goody division, a number of the stores that were on the list (to be closed) are no longer on the list because sales have been improving, or margins have been getting better, or a nearby competitor has closed. So the list of stores to close has been getting smaller."

At the end of the second quarter 1997, Musicland had 1,137 mall stores, consisting of 726 Sam Goody and 411 Suncoast stores. At the end of 1996, the company had 1,199 mall stores, 777 Sam Goody and 422 Suncoast.

At the end of the second quarter 1997, Musicland had 224 superstores, consisting of 156 On Cue and 68 Media Play stores. At the end of 1996, the company had 245 superstores, 158 On Cue and 87 Media Play.
Musicland's last profitable quarter was the fourth quarter of 1995, and a shareholder asked Eugster when the company would see its next profitable quarter.

"I will not forecast," Eugster said. "But this is a highly seasonal business. We often joke that we would be very happy the day we do 100 percent of our profit in the fourth quarter and break even the first three quarters."
Musicland had a net loss of $39.3 million in the first half of 1997, and a net loss of $193.7 million in 1996.
